book.title: Career and Technical Education Grade 7 Student Textbook
book.subject: cte
book.unit_title: Introduction to Career and Technical Education (CTE)

keywords.def: Legal work that gives a service or goods and earns money.
The path of progress a person follows to reach their life goals.

en.text: A job is any legal activity where a person gives a service or produces goods and earns money. It is what a person does now to bring home an income. Cleaner, plumber and teacher are jobs.

screens.title: Earning money
screens.ask: Your neighbour drives a bajaj every day and earns money. What is this called?
screens.after: Legal work that earns money is a job.

screens.title: 1.2 Job vs career
paras: A career is a journey through learning, work and life.
What about a job? Are job and career the same?

screens.title: What a job is
paras: A job is any legal activity that gives a service or produces goods.
In return the person earns money to buy things.
People say: "I have a job as a cleaner." "I have a job as a plumber." "I have a job as a teacher."
They are telling what they do at the moment: their current job.

screens.title: Jobs around you
screens.ask: List the types of jobs in your locality.
screens.answer: Examples: teacher, farmer, shopkeeper, driver, carpenter, tailor, hairdresser, nurse, mechanic, daily labourer.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Legal work that gives a service or goods and earns money.

opts: Working as a plumber for pay
screens.ans: Working as a plumber for pay
screens.why: A job is legal work that earns money.
The book says a job is any legal activity that earns money.
screens.clue: Read the definition of a job.

screens.why: Each earns money by giving a service or producing goods. Watching TV does not.
screens.clue: Does it give a service or goods for money?

screens.text: Does having a job contribute to society?
opts: No, a job only helps the worker
Yes, jobs give services and goods that other people need
screens.ans: Yes, jobs give services and goods that other people need
screens.why: A farmer grows food, a teacher teaches and a nurse cares for the sick. Workers also support their families.
screens.clue: Who uses the goods and services that workers make?

en.text: Job and career are related but different. A job is what you do now for income. It can be short-term. A career is a long-term journey of connected jobs and growth. Getting a job is a one-time event; a career is a lifelong process, like climbing a ladder.

screens.title: Same or different?
screens.after: They are related, but they mean different things. See the table.

screens.title: Table 1.1: Differences between career and job
paras: Career and job are related, but they are different.
table: A series of connected employment opportunities.
Something you do at a particular time.
A satisfying, productive activity through your lifetime.
What you do at work now to bring home income.
A long-term view of many jobs and experiences.
A regular activity in exchange for payment.
A long-term journey based on your passions.
Can be full-time or part-time; may be short-term.
Changes over time as you move between jobs.
Relatively stable; you can work long in it.

screens.title: Climbing a ladder
paras: A career aims to improve your skills so you can grow or move to another job.
Getting a job is a one-time event. A career is a lifelong process.
Progress is like climbing a ladder: elementary, high school, then college or training.
Any work pursued over a long time can be a career. It can even be schoolwork, homemaking or volunteer work.

screens.title: Job and career side by side
defs: What you do now for income. It may be short-term.
A lifelong journey of connected jobs and growth.

items: What I do now for income
screens.why: Career = long-term growth. Job = what you do now.
screens.clue: Ask: is it about now, or about a long path?

screens.text: "I am a grade 7 physics teacher." Does this describe a career or a job?
screens.why: It only tells what the person does at the moment.
screens.clue: Does it show progress over time?

screens.text: "I worked as a recruiting clerk, then assistant personnel head, now personnel manager." Career or job?
screens.why: It shows progress through connected positions in one field.
screens.clue: Look for steps up over time.

screens.text: Career is for immediate gain, but job is future oriented.
screens.why: It is the other way round. A job is for income now; a career is about the future.
screens.clue: Which one is like climbing a ladder?

screens.ask: Getting a job is a one-time event; a ___ is a lifelong process.
screens.why: The book compares a career to climbing a ladder over a lifetime.
screens.clue: Which word means a long path?

screens.text: Selam works in a café on Saturdays to earn pocket money. She dreams of running her own hotel one day and plans to study hotel service. Which is correct?
opts: The café work is her job; the hotel plan is part of her career
The café work is her career
She has neither a job nor a career
screens.ans: The café work is her job; the hotel plan is part of her career
screens.why: The café is what she does now for money, so it is a job. Her long-term path toward running a hotel is her career.
screens.clue: Which part is "now" and which is "future growth"?

items.text: "I have worked as a Home Health Aid, a Nursing Assistant, and a Nurse. I am in health care." Career or job?
items.why: A series of connected jobs with advancement in one field.
items.clue: Look for steps up over time.

items.text: "I am a grade 7 physics teacher." Career or job?
items.why: It tells only the current work.

items.text: "I have worked as a recruiting clerk, an assistant personnel head and now a personnel manager. I am in Human Resource Management." Career or job?
items.why: Progress through positions in one field.

test.why: That is the definition of a job.

test.text: Career and job are not related.
Which is like climbing a ladder?
test.why: A career is a lifelong process of progress.

test.ask: ___ is future-oriented and job is short-term.
test.why: A career looks to future growth; a job may be short-term.

test.text: Dawit was a carpenter's helper, then a carpenter, and now owns a furniture shop. This is an example of:
test.why: Connected jobs with advancement form a career.
